hints.content:
When we make a right triangle with the two points, the distance is the hypotenuse which we can represent with $\greenD x$:



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane with two points on it. The x- and y- axes scale by one. The first point is at three, negative nine. The second point is at six, negative two. A vertical line starts at the first point seven units and a horizontal line three units to the second point. A third line connects both points and is x units making a right triangle. The hypotenuse is x.

hints.content:
Now we can use the Pythagorean theorem to find the distance $\greenD x$:

$\begin{align} \maroonD a^2 + \maroonD b^2 &= \greenD x^2 ~~~~~~~~\small\gray{\text{The Pythagorean theorem}}\\\\
\maroonD{3}^2 + \maroonD{7}^2 &= \greenD{x}^2 ~~~~~~~~\small\gray{\text{Plug in the side lengths}}\\\\
9 + 49 &= \greenD x^2 ~~~~~~~~\small\gray{\text{Evaluate } 3^2 \text{ and }  7^2}\\\\
58 &= \greenD x^2~~~~~~~~\small\gray{\text{Add 9 and 49}}\\\\
\greenD x &= \sqrt{58} ~~~~~~~~\small\gray{\text{Take the square root of each side}}\\\\ \\\end{align}$

###The answer

The distance between the points is $\sqrt{58}$.
